objective: Configuring and troubleshooting resource allocation for a client-side virtual machine
secondaryObjectives: Client-side virtualization concepts: the purpose of a VM and type 1 vs. type 2 hypervisors

sources.cite: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) V15: domains Mobile devices 13%, Networking 23%, Hardware 25%, Virtualization and cloud computing 11%, Hardware and network troubleshooting 28%; launched 2025-03-25
sources.note: Exam page read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-14 ('Diagnosing issues: identifying and fixing hardware, network, and connectivity problems'). The objectives PDF (Exam Objectives Version 1.2) was read in primary text the same day: 5.5 'Given a scenario, troubleshoot network issues' lists 'Limited connectivity' and 'Intermittent internet connectivity'; 2.6 lists APIPA, static and dynamic addressing, subnet mask and gateway; 2.4 lists DHCP leases, reservations, scope and exclusions. The PDF says the troubleshooting methodology 'will not be tested' in the 220-1200 series but remains a competency standard. Reused for REQ-336 from this course's rogue-dhcp-soho-office (the same reading and date); the objective wording is the course seed's.

The business, the users, the devices and the people are fictional. The minutes or days each step takes and the effects of each decision are teaching simplifications for exam practice, not measured values.

brief.situation: You are the help desk technician at Cedarline Software, a fictional software company. A developer's laptop (16 GB RAM, 8 cores, 512 GB SSD) runs a type 2 hypervisor for two test VMs. Three tickets came in from the same developer this morning.
handover: VM A: 12 GB RAM, 6 vCPUs. VM B: 8 GB RAM, 4 vCPUs. Both run at once.
A new laptop for a second developer reports 'virtualization not available' when starting a VM.
howItWorks: The desk shows the ticket queue against the priority matrix and each service's status.
Move on a ticket round at a time. A decision comes to you at each ticket round; before the first, you can read the evidence.
At the end you write the record and a short reflection.

then.log: Round 2: the page file fills the SSD; the host crashes and VM A's disk image is corrupted mid-write.
Round 3: with the TPM cleared, BitLocker demands the recovery key at boot; the developer is locked out for half a day.
Round 4: VM A won't start: its disk chain is broken, and the pre-upgrade state is gone too.

memPrompt.title: More RAM given than the host has
memPrompt.context: Both VMs need to run together for integration tests.

choices.label: Set VM A to 6 GB and 3 vCPUs and VM B to 4 GB and 2 vCPUs, leaving the host about 6 GB and 3 cores, and check the tests still pass

effects.log: Allocations fit the host; nothing pages.

choices.feedback: Allocations must leave the host enough memory and cores for itself and the hypervisor.

choices.label: Tell the developer to run one VM at a time
choices.feedback: No paging, but the integration tests need both.

choices.label: Make the host's page file 64 GB so the allocations 'fit'

effects.log: The page file grows to 64 GB.

choices.feedback: Paging is the slowness; a bigger page file on a nearly full disk makes it worse and fills the disk.

vtxPrompt.title: The hypervisor won't start a VM

choices.label: Enable the CPU's virtualization extensions (Intel VT-x or AMD-V) in the UEFI setup, save, and start the VM

effects.log: Virtualization is enabled; the VM starts.

choices.feedback: Hypervisors need the CPU's virtualization extensions, which ship disabled on some machines.

choices.label: Reinstall the hypervisor
choices.feedback: The hypervisor was fine; the setting is in the firmware.

choices.label: Disable Secure Boot and the TPM to 'unlock' virtualization

effects.log: Secure Boot and the TPM are disabled.

choices.feedback: Those aren't the setting; disabling them suspends BitLocker protection and weakens the laptop for nothing.

snapPrompt.title: 14 snapshots, 4 GB free
snapPrompt.context: The developer needs the snapshot from before last week's database upgrade; the rest are old.

choices.label: Delete the old snapshots in the hypervisor's snapshot manager (it merges them into the disk), keep the pre-upgrade one, and set a snapshot limit
choices.feedback: Snapshots are delta files the hypervisor must merge; delete them through it.

choices.label: Move the whole VM to an external drive
choices.feedback: Space is freed, but the VM now runs slowly from USB and the snapshots keep growing.

choices.label: Delete the snapshot files from the VM's folder in Explorer

effects.log: Snapshot delta files are deleted by hand.

choices.feedback: The running disk depends on that chain of delta files; deleting them by hand breaks the VM.

reflection.question: Write the work notes: how you allocated resources, fixed virtualization support and freed disk space.

parts.label: Allocation
parts.criteria: 20 GB on a 16 GB host caused paging; resized to leave the host room.
parts.modelAnswer: The VMs had 20 GB on a 16 GB host, so it paged; they now have 6 and 4 GB, leaving the host about 6 GB.

parts.label: Firmware and snapshots
parts.criteria: VT-x in UEFI; old snapshots deleted through the hypervisor, pre-upgrade one kept.
parts.modelAnswer: The new laptop needed VT-x enabled in UEFI. Old snapshots were deleted through the snapshot manager, keeping the pre-upgrade one.

memHarm.headline: Allocate what the host has
memHarm.body: VM memory and vCPUs must fit within the host, leaving room for it.

vtxHarm.headline: Change the right setting
vtxHarm.body: Virtualization extensions are a firmware setting; leave Secure Boot and the TPM alone.

snapHarm.headline: Manage snapshots in the hypervisor
snapHarm.body: Delete snapshots through the hypervisor, which merges them safely.

target.headline: Good: vMs that fit their host
target.body: Allocations within the host, the right firmware setting, and snapshots managed by the hypervisor.

scoring.modelReasoning: A type 2 hypervisor runs on the host OS, so VM memory and vCPUs must fit within the host and leave it room; over-allocation pages to disk. Hypervisors need the CPU's virtualization extensions (VT-x or AMD-V) enabled in firmware. Snapshots are chains of delta files that the hypervisor merges when you delete one; deleting files by hand breaks the disk.
